videos.title: My son & his fiance charcoal portrait
videos.description:
This was a last minute Christmas gift idea to create a portrait for my son Richie and his fiancé Christina. I actually got inspired to do this since I just saw them at our Christmas party and he gave me a beautiful picture of both of them. So I decided I would surprise them and do a portrait of them using the picture as the subject. I just pulled an all-nighter to get it in time for Christmas but I'm happy how it came out considering the time restraint. 

This was done on an 11x14 inch Utrecht Premium 2-Ply Bristol paper. I used General's charcoal pencils (2B, 4B and 6B) for the sketch and a flat paint brush to put in charcoal powder for the background.

videos.title: Critiqued acrylic painting of my daughter Arianna 16x20
videos.description:
After a few months of deliberating over how to fix a portrait that I previously painted of my daughter Arianna, I decided to finally go ahead and give it a try. I was originally scared that I might ruin it but I'm glad that I took the chance. I believe it's a much better likeness of her. 

These are the few areas which I have fixed:

1. Her left jaw line.
2. Shadow areas around jaw, neck and hairline.
3. Lightened up the area around her eyes.
4. Allowed her lower left side of face to show through her hair. This was the 2nd biggest improvement!
5. Removed and softened up her right cheek bone which was making her look much older than she was in the picture. This was the biggest improvement! 
6. Lightened up her blonde hair and added highlights.

Here's the link to the first part of this painting before the critique:
https://youtu.be/BxYVa_vR2Ks

videos.title: (Part 1) Acrylic painting portrait of my daughter Arianna at 9 years old
videos.description:
Update 8/5/2018: I finally got the nerve to critique this painting since I was not happy with the way it came out initially. After watching this (part 1) video, you can watch the new (part 2) critiqued version here:

https://youtu.be/r1XfYw-RRsU

I finally finished my daughter Arianna's portrait. The picture was taken last year in 2016 which would make her 9 years old this year. This is my first attempt at a portrait painting so please be kind lol. No one ever said that painting portraits in acrylics would be easy. It was done on a large 16x20 inch canvas which was much bigger than the 8x10 photograph that I that I used as my subject. Hope you like it.
